    max_x = max(point[0] for point in points)

A standard approach for point-in-polygon tests uses barycentric coordinates. The point lies inside or on an edge if and only if the sum of the three small areas equals the large area, and furthermore none of the small areas is negative. To avoid a floating-point comparison in a loop, I compute the sum and the bound in the same exact expression: I return True exactly when twice the large area equals the sum of twice each small area.

    def point_in_triangle(p, a, b, c):
        # Twice the signed area of the whole triangle
        whole = (b[0] - a[0]) * (c[1] - a[1]) - (c[0] - a[0]) * (b[1] - a[1])
        # Twice the signed areas of the three small triangles
        abp = (b[0] - a[0]) * (p[1] - a[1]) - (p[0] - a[0]) * (b[1] - a[1])
        bcp = (c[0] - b[0]) * (p[1] - b[1]) - (p[0] - b[0]) * (c[1] - b[1])
        cap = (a[0] - c[0]) * (p[1] - c[1]) - (p[0] - c[0]) * (a[1] - c[1])
